findings.body: The deleteMany call for the SMS cron endpoint would silently remove EMAIL/WHATSAPP workflow reminders that happen to have retryCount>1, even though this endpoint is documented and intended to operate only on scheduled SMS reminders, causing unrelated reminder data loss.
findings.failure_mode: Overly broad database delete criteria causing unintended data loss for non-SMS reminder rows sharing the same column.
findings.impact: The deleteMany call for the SMS cron endpoint would silently remove EMAIL/WHATSAPP workflow reminders that happen to have retryCount>1, even though this endpoint is documented and intended to operate only on scheduled SMS reminders, causing unrelated reminder data loss.
findings.root_cause: The new retryCount-based delete condition was added as an unscoped OR branch instead of being combined with the method filter.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the retryCount branch of the OR array so the deletion only ever targets SMS reminders.
findings.title: Retry-count deletion filter not scoped to SMS method, risking cross-method deletions
findings.trigger: Any WorkflowReminder row (EMAIL or WHATSAPP method) whose shared retryCount column is ever set above 1 by other code paths, or by manual/db-level updates, since retryCount is a column on the whole WorkflowReminder model, not an SMS-only field.
findings.verifier_reason: The patch adds an OR branch at lines 38-42 with only `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` and no `method` filter. This deleteMany will remove any WorkflowReminder row (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, or SMS) where retryCount > 1, not just SMS reminders. The code is in scheduleSMSReminders.ts which is intended for SMS only. The trigger is realistic: any reminder type with retryCount > 1 gets deleted.

pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

Right now when SMS fails to send because of whatever reason (e.g. invalid phone number), we are trying to keep scheduling it in our corn job until the date is reached. This PR introduces a retry count, after scheduling failed twice we delete the workflow reminder.
pr.title: fix: add retryCount to workflowReminder

raw_findings.root_cause: The OR/retryCount branch was added without updating the explanatory comment describing the query's purpose.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Update the comment above the deleteMany call to also mention the new retryCount-based deletion condition.
raw_findings.title: Stale comment no longer describes the updated deleteMany query semantics
raw_findings.trigger: A reviewer or maintainer reads the unmodified comment 'delete all scheduled sms reminders where scheduled date is past current date' above this block and assumes the delete is solely date-driven.

raw_findings.body: No automated test verifies that retryCount is incremented on failure or that reminders are deleted after exceeding the retry threshold, allowing regressions in this new failure-handling behavior to go unnoticed.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Silent regressions in retry/deletion behavior due to missing verification.
raw_findings.impact: No automated test verifies that retryCount is incremented on failure or that reminders are deleted after exceeding the retry threshold, allowing regressions in this new failure-handling behavior to go unnoticed.
raw_findings.root_cause: New retry logic was introduced without accompanying test cases.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add unit/integration tests covering: (1) retryCount increments when scheduleSMS returns falsy, (2) retryCount increments on thrown errors, and (3) deleteMany removes reminders once retryCount exceeds the threshold.
raw_findings.title: No test coverage added for new retry-count increment/deletion logic
raw_findings.trigger: Running the handler in cases where scheduleSMS returns falsy or throws, to exercise the retryCount increment path and the eventual deleteMany threshold behavior.

raw_findings.impact: Divergence between the two duplicated update blocks over time could lead to inconsistent retry-count handling between the 'scheduling returned falsy' path and the 'exception thrown' path.
raw_findings.root_cause: The same prisma update call for incrementing retryCount was copy-pasted into two branches instead of being factored into a shared helper.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Extract the retryCount increment `prisma.workflowReminder.update` call into a small helper function and call it from both the else branch and the catch block.
